nodes.summary: A sequent $A \vdash B$ is derivable in RC if and only if it is true in every Kripke model on an RC-frame.
nodes.title: Kripke completeness of RC

nodes.summary: RC derives sequents $A \vdash B$ between strictly positive formulas from the axioms and rules
nodes.title: The Reflection Calculus RC

nodes.summary: There is a map $o$ from worms to ordinals such that two worms are RC-equivalent iff they have the same value, $\alpha <_0 \beta$ iff $o(\alpha) < o(\beta)$, and the values are exactly the ordinals below $\varepsilon_0$. Equivalently, worms modulo RC-equivalence, ordered by $<_0$, are order-isomorphic to $(\varepsilon_0, <)$. The value is computed recursively: $o(0^k) = k$; otherwise, if…
nodes.title: Worms have order type `ε₀`

nodes.summary: The strictly positive formulas of the Reflection Calculus are generated by with $p$ ranging over atoms. There is no negation, disjunction or box. The source also allows a modality $\omega$ (full uniform reflection); it is omitted here.
nodes.title: Strictly positive formulas

nodes.summary: A family of relations $(R_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ on a set $W$ is an RC-frame when, for all $x, y, z \in W$ and $m, n \in \mathbb{N}$:
nodes.title: RC-frame

nodes.summary: For every $k$, $\langle 1 \rangle\top \vdash \langle 0 \rangle\langle 0 \rangle^k\top$ in RC, that is $0^k <_0 1$. In the ordinal assignment of worms, $0^k$ has value $k$ and $1$ has value $\omega$.
nodes.title: The worms `0⋯0` lie below the worm `1`

nodes.summary: In a Kripke model with relations $(R_n)$ and valuation $V$: $x \Vdash p$ iff $p \in V(x)$; $x \Vdash \top$ always; $x \Vdash A \wedge B$ iff $x \Vdash A$ and $x \Vdash B$; and $x \Vdash \langle n \rangle A$ iff some $y$ with $x R_n y$ satisfies $A$. A sequent $A \vdash B$ is true in the model when every world satisfying $A$ satisfies $B$.
nodes.title: Truth of a strictly positive formula in a Kripke model

nodes.summary: If $A \vdash B$ is derivable in RC, then $A \vdash B$ is true in every Kripke model on an RC-frame.
nodes.title: Soundness of RC for RC-models

nodes.summary: If $A \vdash B$ is derivable in RC, then $C[A/p] \vdash C[B/p]$ is derivable for every strictly positive formula $C$ and atom $p$. Since all connectives are monotone, no polarity condition is needed.
nodes.title: Positive replacement

nodes.summary: For strictly positive formulas $C$ and $A$ and an atom $p$, $C[A/p]$ replaces every occurrence of $p$ in $C$ by $A$. The result is again strictly positive.
nodes.title: Substitution in strictly positive formulas

nodes.summary: If $A \vdash B$ is derivable in RC, then so is $A[C/p] \vdash B[C/p]$, for every strictly positive $C$ and atom $p$: RC is a normal positive logic.
nodes.title: Closure under substitution

nodes.summary: For worms $\alpha$ and $\beta$, $\alpha <_0 \beta$ means $\beta \vdash \langle 0 \rangle\alpha$ in RC: arithmetically, the reflection principle $\beta$ proves the consistency of $\alpha$. The source defines it in GLP by $\mathrm{GLP} \vdash \beta \to \langle 0 \rangle\alpha$; the two definitions agree by Dashkov's theorem.
nodes.title: The order `<₀` on worms

nodes.summary: A worm is a closed strictly positive formula without conjunction, $\langle n_1 \rangle \langle n_2 \rangle \cdots \langle n_k \rangle \top$, written as the word $n_1 n_2 \cdots n_k$; the empty word is $\top$. Every closed strictly positive formula is equivalent to a worm.
nodes.title: Worm

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
